proposed.text: A light manufacturing facility (moderate fire risk) is proposed to be converted into a daycare center for 80 children (high life risk, low fire risk). Applying the two criteria of Sec. 702, how should the Building Official classify this change?

options.text: Less hazardous overall — fire risk decreases so the BO may approve at discretion without full Code review, provided no other factors increase risk
More hazardous overall — life risk increases substantially with 80 vulnerable child occupants, triggering mandatory full Code compliance
Equivalent hazard — the decrease in fire risk exactly offsets the increase in life risk so no review is needed, assuming no additional hazards are present
Outside Code jurisdiction — daycare centers are regulated exclusively by DSWD, not by PD 1096

proposed.rationale: Sec. 702 requires evaluation of BOTH life risk AND fire risk. While fire risk decreases (daycare vs. manufacturing), life risk increases substantially: 80 young children are among the most vulnerable occupants, requiring enhanced egress design, fire detection, supervision, and accessibility features. A significant increase in life risk — even when fire risk decreases — classifies the change as more hazardous overall, mandating full Code compliance. Option C assumes the two criteria cancel out, which has no basis in the Code.
proposed.explanation: When life risk and fire risk point in different directions, the more conservative interpretation governs. Vulnerable occupants (children, elderly, persons with disabilities) elevate life risk regardless of fire hazard level. Full Code compliance is required whenever either criterion indicates increased hazard.
